scope: two owned Android API36 AOSP ARM64 and one iOS26.5 iPhone17Pro simulator; production MessagePage/controllers, OS vault and encrypted SQLite; production API/outbox/receipt processes with PG/Redis; synthetic refresh IdP, not customer interactive SSO

production_change.behavior: successful read ACK notifies active view and clears only its identical read failure; newer unrelated errors retained; marker cleared on context change
production_change.regression: two actual RED then GREEN controller cases plus actual Android/iOS warning-absence assertions and screenshots

fault_scope: fixture pre-forward503 only for explicit Bob Android/iOS delivered/read paths; no fabricated success; body SHA256 and monotonic request arrival time only, no proof/token body saved; each flow held until at least two real automatic attempts, then released to production API
delivery_scope: actual encrypted SQLite page committed cursor1 and pending proof before delivery200; delivery503 keeps page pending and does not grant visible/read authority; after automatic success pending cleared and no read before actual visible UI
failure_observation_scope: passive observer delegates exact real HttpApiTransport request/cancellation/response, records received503/device/action; SyncCoordinator retries transient delivered failures silently without onFailure, so view.failure is not a transport error log; view transition diagnostics also retained
read_scope: visible UI real500ms exposure and batching; read503 leaves device local read set and DB read empty; Retry-After2 honored on automatic retries; iOS release marks only its device read, Android remains locally unread despite aggregate user-read1; Android later success deduplicates same user read
recovery_scope: same installed native processes and admitted devices throughout; no manual refresh, reselect, retry button, process restart or injected ACK; exact request body digest matches failed and first successful delivery/read attempt; normal seq2 reply and seq3 send converge afterwards

visual_review.method: direct visual inspection of five actual native screenshots
observations: iOS read failure displays actual warning and unread1 while body remains visible
after automatic read success iOS and Android warning removed, unread0, same message once
sender shows delivered before recipient read recovery
after recovery final sender view shows three distinct messages, own seq1 and seq3 read badges

limitations: controlled transient503 before forwarding, not authorization failure or every HTTP status
delivery uses existing exponential RetryPolicy; read503 uses Retry-After2, no claim that delivery503 honors Retry-After
read queue retry tested in same native process, not durable read exposure across death/reboot
receipt ACK loss after server commit is not this controlled failure window
no physical hardware, four-platform full acceptance, customer SSO, signed distribution, push notifications or remote CI claim
